findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State that excluding .github/release-requirements.txt removes its Dependabot coverage, and name the replacement path (e.g., a manual recompile cadence or a follow-up ticket) plus the revert path (remove the exclude-paths entry).

No mention of how release-requirements.txt will be kept current after exclusion.
findings.finding: The fix excludes .github/release-requirements.txt from the Dependabot uv update. Dependabot will no longer recompile or bump that file, so its pinned dependencies lose automated updates, including security bumps. The plan does not acknowledge this behavior change. It also names no replacement mechanism, such as a separate ecosystem entry, a manual recompile step, or a follow-up ticket, and no back-out path.
scenarios: A CVE lands in a package pinned in release-requirements.txt and no Dependabot PR is ever opened for it.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State the consequence of excluding .github/release-requirements.txt from Dependabot and name how that file's pins will stay current (or explicitly accept and track the gap).

Absence: no statement of who or what now updates .github/release-requirements.txt.
findings.finding: Excluding .github/release-requirements.txt from Dependabot changes existing behavior. That file will no longer receive automated dependency updates. The plan does not acknowledge this or say how the release requirements will be kept current. Options include a separate manual or scheduled recompile, a separate Dependabot ecosystem entry, or an accepted staleness.
scenarios: Pins in .github/release-requirements.txt (used by release tooling) silently drift and miss security updates, because Dependabot now skips them.

findings.finding: The plan doesn't record what the chosen exclusion costs. `.github/**` is a broad glob. It takes .github/release-requirements.txt, and any requirements-shaped file added under .github/ later, out of Dependabot's automated uv version updates. The plan never says that this is intended or what keeps the release lock current instead.

findings.finding:
The plan body never states the root cause or the fix.
- The Observation says 'The log does not name the files in the rejected payload'.
- The root cause (that .github/release-requirements.txt was recompiled into the payload and rejected) appears only inside AC1's provenance parenthetical.
- The fix (adding exclude-paths to dependabot.yml) appears only indirectly in the Testing section.
- AC1 claims the rejected file was identified, but the plan never says which file or explains the inference. The evidence cited is a correlation: the file was recompiled in both failing runs. The 400 itself does not name it.
scenarios: A future reader or reviewer cannot tell from the plan which file was rejected, why a .github/ file is refused by Dependabot's API, or what exclude-paths entry was added.
The root-cause claim rests on correlation (file recompiled in both failing runs), confirmed only by the post-fix run; this inference chain is unstated.

findings.location: Plan body (no Approach/Fix section); Testing paragraph

findings.suggested_fix: Add: '## Fix\nExclude `.github/**` from the uv Dependabot entry (`exclude-paths`). The uv scan treats requirements-shaped files under the directory as pip manifests and recompiled .github/release-requirements.txt into the uv-lock group; Dependabot's API rejects that change with 400. That file is a hand-regenerated release-build lock, so excluding it removes the rejected change without losing any intended automation.'
